name: sprouts_search
description:
THE DEFAULT TOOL. Find companies, people or documents matching a DESCRIPTION of who to find. A natural-language `query` is the primary interface; `filters` is a vetted override, never a place to restate the query. "Who works at X" is this tool with `category: "person"`.

Read the result before reporting it. `interpreted_as` shows the filters the engine actually applied (`source: "parser"` means it inferred them from your words), and `caveats` lists what it could not do. When `total_is_estimate` is true, `total` is a floor: say "at least N", never an exact count. `has_more` with a `next_cursor` means more rows exist. An empty result means nothing matched what was applied, not that the entity does not exist: the index does not hold every company or person, and some categories have no index in a given deployment.

Filter values must come from the live vocabulary. Seniority is exactly `C-Suite`, `VP`, `Director / Head`, `Manager`, `IC`, `Entry`, `In Training`. Industries look like `Software & Technology`; departments like `Marketing` or `Engineering / Software`. Founders, owners, partners, investors and advisors are `governance_level`, and consultants and freelancers are `employment_type`, not seniorities. An invented filter name or value fails the whole call: move that constraint into the `query` words instead.

Billed per result: the first 10 results cost 0.5 credits with `mode: "fast"` or 0.595 with `auto`, and each extra result 0.08 or 0.085. A later page costs only the results it adds, and a search that finds nothing is free. `environment: "test"` in a result means a test key: real records, zero credits.

description_hints.sprouts_entity_lookup: To get a row's full record, call sprouts_entity_lookup with the row's `lookup` value: a company by its domain with `by: "domain"`, a person by their LinkedIn URL with `by: "li_url"`. Never pass a row's `id`: search ids cannot be looked up.

refused_arguments.page: This tool has no `page`. Pass `cursor` from the previous result's `next_cursor` instead.
refused_arguments.offset: This tool has no `offset`. Pass `cursor` from the previous result's `next_cursor` instead.
refused_arguments.updated_after: `updated_after` is not implemented and would fail at execution. Remove it.

query.description: Natural language: the primary interface, and never the wrong choice. Describe the ideal record, not keywords: "payments companies in Germany with 500-5000 staff" beats "fintech DE". Optional if `filters` is given.

category.description: What to search, and the type of every row returned. Pick the category the ANSWER lives in: "companies hiring Rust engineers" is `job_opening`, "who leads security at Acme" is `person`. `auto` lets the engine choose; it needs `mode: "auto"` and a `query`, and accepts no `filters`, domains or `sort`.

mode.description: `fast` (about 1-2 s) matches literally and does NO query parsing: a country, headcount or industry stated only in words is silently not applied. `auto` (about 12 s, more credits) has a model turn your words into filters. Use `fast` when the constraints are in `filters`, `auto` when they live in the sentence.

filters.description: Structured constraints for `company` and `person` searches. Most calls need only `query`. Anything set here overrides what the parser would infer. Do not copy names out of a result's `interpreted_as`: it echoes the engine's internal names.

technology.description: Technologies a company uses, for example `HubSpot` or `AWS`.

geo.description: Location, the only geography filter: {"places":[{"value":"germany","level":"country"}]}. There is no `country` or `city` filter.

negate.description: Exclude this place instead of requiring it.

last_funding_date.description: When the latest round closed, both bounds inclusive: ISO dates (`2024-01-01`) or date math (`now-90d`).

seniority.description: Exactly 7 levels, most senior first: `C-Suite`, `VP`, `Director / Head`, `Manager`, `IC`, `Entry`, `In Training`. `Director` and `Head` are ONE level.

department.description: Function labels, for example `Marketing`, `Sales`, `Engineering / Software`, `IT & Infrastructure`, `Data, Analytics & AI`.

governance_level.description: Board and ownership roles, for founder, owner and investor questions: `Founder`, `Co Founder`, `Owner`, `Partner`, `Board Member`, `Investor`, `Advisor`.

employment_type.description: How someone is engaged: `Full Time`, `Part Time`, `Freelancer`, `Contractor`, `Consultant (External)`.

sort.description: Order the results, strongest key first. Omit it for the engine's own ordering, which is right for most searches; use it when the user asked for an extreme ("the largest", "most recently funded"). Sortable fields differ per category and an unknown one fails the call, so do not guess a field name.

include_domains.description: Restrict to these company domains. `company`, `person` and `job_opening` only.

exclude_domains.description: Leave out these company domains. `company`, `person` and `job_opening` only.

limit.description: Rows per page. The application may cap it lower; the result says so in `caveats`.

cursor.description: From a previous result's `next_cursor`. Resend the same request unchanged plus the cursor: it is bound to every other field except `limit`. Cursors expire after 24 hours.

fields.description: Return only these record fields (plus `id` and `category`). Omit for a compact default set; a field missing from a row may simply not be in that set, so ask for it by name.
